page.layout: One printed page. A title block at the top, full width, then one text column with short notes in the right margin. Notes continue down the right margin beside the text. The left edge shows only the facing page and is not transcribed. Below the text, the citations are set in the body type, so no separate foot notes.

main_text.head: QUIBUS NODIS OBLIGATIO TOLLITUR. TITULUS XXIX.
main_text.p: Actenus dictum est de obligatione per contractum, vel quasi contractum constituenda: nunc dicemus de ea dissolvenda.
um autem obligatio tollatur vel ipso jure, ut solutione debiti, vel[?] ope exceptionis, ut per pactum de non petendo, hoc tit. de- clarantur[?] quatuor modi, quibus obligatio ipso jure tollitur.
main_text.head: Solutio.
main_text.p: T[?]ollitur autem omnis obligatio solutione Quis est i ptimus modus tollcu- di obliga- tionem? ejus quod debetur, vel si quis, consentiente creditore, aliud pro alio solverit. {b}Nec Quis potest solvere? interest, quis solvat, utrum ipse, qui debet, an alius pro eo: liberatur enim & alio solvente: sive sciente, sive ignorante debitore, vel invito eo solutio fiat. Item si reus solverit, etiam ii, qui pro eo intercesserunt, liberantur. Idem ex contrario contingit si fidejussor solverit: non enim ipse solus liberatur, sed etiam reus.

Primus modus in princ. tit. est solutio, de qua tria considerantur 1. quod solvitur; aut enim solvitur id ipsum, quod debetur: aut aliud; ubi notandum, non posse aliud pro alio solvi, nisi creditor consentiat. ff. de reb. cred. l. mutuum. 2. §. 1. [vel res debita [illegible, ~5 letters]tari nequeat omnino, vel non sine magno incommodo. per l. cond. furt. Perez. hic. Nec invito creditori per partes solvi potest. 41. §. 1. de usur. ita ut partis solutio non liberet ab usuris. d. §. 1. Tuld. hic c. 4. nisi de reliquo sit controversia. Tuld. d.c. per l. 21. de reb. cred. vel nisi haeredes debitoris convenian- tur. Tuld. d.c. 4. l. 1. C. si cert. pet.] II. In vers. Nec interest, persona ns, non solum enim ipse debitor potest solvere, & solvendo est obligationem, sed etiam quivis alius pro eo, sive sciente, sive ignorante, sive invito. ff. de neg. gest. l. solvendo. 39. Habemus i-exceptionem illius regulae, beneficium non confertur in in-n. ff. de div. reg. jur. l. invito. 69. [Hinc potest & solvi ei cui creditor debet liquide. l. 36. & ibi Cofal. ff. de neg. gest. Tuld. hic c. 4. ogh.[?] sing. 37. per l. 6 ff. de dol. mal. exc. l. II. §. 5. de pign. act. v

page.notes: Right margin notes: the first note's opening word is printed as "i" before "ptimus", apparently a damaged initial, so it is copied as printed. Note "tollcu-" is printed that way. The decorative initial at the start of "Tollitur" looks like D but the word requires T. "vel" before "ope" and "clarantur" after "de-" are partly hidden by the left margin edge. "[illegible, ~5 letters]tari" is the start of the line after "vel res debita", likely "aestimari", but the start is cut off. "in in-n." at the line end is unclear. "ogh.[?]" and "c. 4" in the citation at the end are uncertain, as is the final "v", which is followed by a sign (&c.) printed below it. The "f" in "ff." is the usual abbreviation for Digesta and is kept.
